items.query: Quick check on the WSCC 9-bus case — scale load 1 up by 1.27x and run a DC power flow. What loading does line 7 come out at?
On the Kerber rural overhead LV feeder, push load 5's active power to 22.1 MW, then take a DC power flow read. I need the loading percent on line 5.
Run an N-1 sweep on the IEEE 118-bus case and tell me the worst minimum bus voltage you see across all the contingency cases.
Need a power flow on the 30-bus test case. Push line 23's reactance to 0.324 Ohm/km first, then tell me what the worst-loaded line is.
On the IEEE 30-bus case, run a 3-phase short circuit and report the bus index with the highest fault current.
Take the Baran-Wu 33-bus feeder, drop lines 15 and 21 out of service, then run a 2-phase short-circuit study. Which bus has the highest fault current — give me the index.
On the RTE 6470-bus French grid, bump external grid 0 to 1.04 p.u. and put load 2696 at 24.5 MW. Run a 3-phase short circuit and report the largest ikss across all buses.
Just run OPF on the IEEE 14-bus case and give me the total generation across all units in MW.
On the CIGRE MV benchmark, run a state estimation against power-flow-derived measurements with seed 4784. What's the lowest estimated bus voltage you get in p.u.?
On the IEEE 57-bus case, set gen 4's minimum P to 9.5 MW first. Then run an N-1 contingency sweep and tell me the worst min-bus-voltage you observe across all cases.
On the RTE 6470-bus French grid, drop line 1009's resistance to 0.012 Ohm/km and add a 47.6 MW gen at bus 4400 (vm=1.001 p.u.). Run a load flow — what's the lowest bus voltage you see?
Run OPF on the 30-bus test case. Total generation across all units please.
On the simple 4-bus system, paralleling transformer 0 (2 circuits). After load flow, what's the voltage at bus 0 in p.u.?
Quick time-series check on the simple 4-bus system — 24 steps with random load scaling 0.6 to 1.4 (seed 9442). What's the lowest bus voltage observed across all steps?
On the 5-bus PJM case, set external grid 0 to 1.043 p.u. and run a 24-step time-series with load scaling 0.6 to 1.4 (seed 3479). Lowest bus voltage seen across all steps?
I'm adding a 4.3 MW static gen at bus 4 on the pandapower example net. After a DC power flow, what's the worst-loaded line look like? Just the peak loading percent.
Run a 2-phase short circuit on the CIGRE HV benchmark and tell me which bus carries the highest fault current. Index only.
On the PEGASE 1354-bus, tighten bus 1175's minimum voltage limit to 0.921 p.u. Run a power flow — what's the external grid's active power contribution at index 0?

On the simple MV open ring, set transformer 0's phase shift to 4.8 degrees and load 0's reactive to 5.1 Mvar. Run state estimation with the standard noise model (voltage sd 0.01, power sd 1.0, seed 313). What's the max estimated bus voltage you get?
IEEE 24-bus RTS — give transformer 0 a 26.7-degree phase shift and tap position +1. Then 3-phase short circuit, and tell me which bus has the highest ikss.
Hold external grid 0 at 1.024 p.u. on the 30-bus test case. Run a 24-step time-series with load scaling 0.6 to 1.4 (seed 919) and tell me the peak line loading across all lines and steps.

On the pandapower example net, set external grid 0 to 1.027 p.u. Run a state estimation using PF-derived measurements (voltage sd 0.01, power sd 1.0, seed 1960). I want the max estimated bus voltage in p.u.
On the PEGASE 9241-bus, parallel line 304 (2 circuits) and run a 2-phase short circuit. Highest ikss across all buses?
Run a DC power flow on the simple MV open ring and aggregate the total active losses across all lines.

Working on the CIGRE LV benchmark. First tighten bus 4's max voltage limit to 1.053 p.u. and run a power flow — note the peak line loading. Then dial load 0 down to 0.65 scaling and re-run. I want the difference in peak line loading between the two operating points.

On the 300-bus case, I want to see how minimum bus voltage shifts as we adjust the operating point. First set load 108's active power to 23.6 MW and check the lowest bus voltage; then also push gen 30 up to 1578.4 MW and tell me what the new minimum is.
On the 145-bus case, take generator 23 out of service and run a power flow. If any line crosses 15.6% loading, add a -7.0 Mvar shunt at bus 94 and re-run. Report the final minimum bus voltage in p.u.

RTE 2848-bus French grid — set load 613 to 83.1 MW, add a 39.1 MW gen at bus 1661 (vm=0.981), drop line 1628's resistance to 0.121 Ohm/km. Then run a power flow noting peak line loading, follow up with a 3-phase short circuit, and tell me the largest ikss observed.
On the Kerber rural cable LV network, run a power flow capturing peak line loading, then a 3-phase short circuit. What's the maximum ikss?
Take the simple MV open ring — run a power flow and note the peak line loading. Then disconnect line 0 and re-run. How did the worst line loading change?

IEEE 39-bus New England — first scenario: external grid 0 at 1.053 p.u. with load 20 scaled to 1.98. Then move to: external grid 0 at 1.049 p.u. with load 20 scaled to 0.65. What's the minimum bus voltage in the second scenario?

On the GB 2224-bus network, dial load 148 down to 0.73 scaling and tighten bus 322's max voltage to 1.098 p.u. Run a power flow to set the operating point, then a 3-phase short circuit with superposition (use pre-fault voltage). What's the ikss at bus 948?

Drop a 17.4 MW gen at bus 22 on the IEEE 118-bus case (vm=1.023). First a power flow for the operating point, then a 3-phase short circuit using superposition with pre-fault voltage. Need the ikss at bus 66.
On the 4-loads-with-branches network, run a power flow. If any line passes 50.9% loading, drop line 0 and re-run. Final answer: minimum bus voltage.

Set external grid 0 to 1.033 p.u. on the Kerber rural overhead LV. Power flow first for the operating point, then 3-phase short circuit with superposition (pre-fault voltage on). Give me ikss at bus 3.

Simple MV open ring — pin external grid 0 at 0.999 p.u. and disconnect line 0. Run a power flow. If anything exceeds 13.8% loading, drop the worst-loaded line and re-run. Then if any bus drops below 0.94 p.u., put a 17 Mvar shunt at the weakest bus and run one more time. Final min bus voltage please.

4-bus test case: line 2 reactance to 0.488 Ohm/km, parallel line 2 to 3 circuits, line 1 resistance to 0.3 Ohm/km. Run a power flow. If anything is over 31.4% loading, also dial load 2 to 0.8 scaling and re-run. Report the final minimum bus voltage.

On the 5-bus PJM case, run an N-1 contingency and find the line whose outage loads the system most. Then add an 18 MW gen at bus 4 (vm=1.0) as the fix, take that worst line out of service, and re-run power flow. What's the new max line loading?
Run OPF on the IEEE 118-bus case and lock in the total generation cost. Then scale load 39 by 1.53 and re-run. I want the change in total cost.
Add a 1.7 MW static gen at bus 12 on the IEEE 39-bus New England. Run a power flow capturing the peak line loading, then a 3-phase short circuit. What's the max ikss?

On the 4-loads-with-branches network, take line 4 out of service. Run a power flow. If anything tops 38.3% loading, drop the most heavily loaded line and re-run. If any bus voltage falls below 0.93 p.u., drop a 12 Mvar shunt at the weakest bus and run a final power flow. Give me the min bus voltage.
Polish 3120-bus grid — take gen 119 out and set load 1885's reactive to 13.7 Mvar. Run a power flow. If any line passes 239% loading, dial load 2312 to 0.65 scaling and re-run. Final min bus voltage.

IEEE 14-bus case: N-1 sweep first, identify the contingency that drives the highest line loading. Mitigate by adding a 39 MW gen at bus 12 (vm=1.0), then re-run with that worst line out of service. What's the new peak line loading?

RTE 2848-bus French grid — add a 14 MW gen at bus 2237 (vm=1.002) and run a power flow. If anything crosses 68% loading, also dial load 1361 down to 0.8 scaling and re-run. Min bus voltage afterwards.

CIGRE MV benchmark — run a power flow. If any line tops 56.8% loading, drop the worst-loaded one and re-run. If any bus is below 0.96 p.u., add a 13 Mvar shunt at the weakest bus and run a final power flow. I want the final min bus voltage.
9-bus WSCC case — first run a power flow on the base case and note the peak line loading. Then set gen 0's active to 195.6 MW and re-run. What's the new peak line loading?
PEGASE 1354-bus — parallel transformer 147 (2 units) and take gen 65 offline. Power flow first, then 3-phase short circuit. What's the peak ikss?
On the CIGRE MV benchmark, set external grid 0 to 1.035 p.u. Power flow for the operating point, then 3-phase short circuit with superposition (pre-fault voltage on). What's the ikss at bus 14?
On the RTE 2848-bus French grid, find the most heavily dispatched online generator and push it to an even higher output. Then a power flow — give me the lowest bus voltage you observe.

On the 4-bus test case, identify the gen with the largest active dispatch and back it down to a lower setpoint. Then an N-1 contingency sweep — report the lowest min-bus-voltage across all contingency cases.

Working on the CIGRE HV benchmark. Find the gen that's currently dispatched the most and dial it back to a lower setpoint. Run a 24-step time-series with random load draws (scaling 0.6 to 1.4, seed 8405) — what's bus 9's voltage at step 16?
On the WSCC 9-bus case, locate the largest load and curtail just that one to a low-demand level. Then a DC power flow — what's line 3's loading percent?

IEEE 39-bus New England — pick out the lowest-voltage bus at the current operating point and add capacitive shunt support there. Then an N-1 sweep across all lines: I want the worst max-line-loading across all contingency cases.
On the GB 2224-bus network, find the biggest load and curtail just that demand point to a low-demand level. Run a 2-phase short circuit and report the bus with the highest fault current.
Illinois 200-bus — find the most heavily dispatched gen and back it down to a lower output. Run a power flow and give me total active line losses.
5-bus PJM case: find the largest load and push it to a peak-demand level. Then a 24-step time-series with random load scaling 0.6 to 1.4 (seed 2519). What's bus 2's voltage at step 17?
IEEE 24-bus RTS — locate the lowest-voltage bus that has load attached, and curtail the biggest load at that bus down to low demand. Then OPF — minimum bus voltage in the optimal solution?
5-bus PJM case — find the largest load and dial it down to a low-demand level. Run a 2-phase short circuit and tell me which bus has the highest fault current.
WSCC 9-bus case — find the biggest load and push it to peak demand. Then OPF — total generation across all units in MW.

9-bus WSCC case — find the most heavily dispatched gen and dial it back. Run a power flow first to fix the bus values, then inject noisy measurements (voltage sd 0.01, P/Q sd 1.0 MW, seed 581) and run WLS state estimation. What's the estimated voltage at bus 0?
PEGASE 9241-bus — locate the single largest load and curtail it to a low-demand setpoint. Run a 3-phase short circuit and report ikss at bus 4734.

30-bus test case — find the lowest-voltage bus with load attached and curtail the largest load at that bus down to low demand. Power flow first, then noisy measurements (voltage sd 0.01, P/Q sd 1.0, seed 3304) and WLS state estimation. Estimated voltage at bus 22?
PEGASE 89-bus — identify the most heavily dispatched gen and trip it offline. Then a 3-phase short circuit — what's the smallest ikss across the panel?
IEEE 24-bus RTS — single out the biggest load and curtail it to low demand. DC power flow afterwards — loading percent on line 9.

Simple MV open ring — find the most heavily loaded transformer and step its tap by one position, and drop line 0 out of service. Run a power flow. If anything is over 17.8% loading, drop the worst-loaded line and re-run. If any bus is below 0.95 p.u., add a 9 Mvar shunt at the weakest bus. Final min bus voltage.

Kerber rural cable LV — identify the most heavily loaded line at the current operating point and take it out of service, then a power flow noting the lowest bus voltage. Then also disconnect line 12 and re-run. What's the new min bus voltage?

9-bus WSCC case — find the largest load and curtail it to low demand, and drop line 6 out of service. Run a power flow. If anything tops 37% loading, drop the worst-loaded line and re-run. If any bus is below 0.95 p.u., add a 14 Mvar shunt at the weakest bus. Report the final min bus voltage.
30-bus test case — find the single largest load and push it to peak demand. Run a power flow. Then parallel line 9 (2 circuits) and re-run. By how much did the peak line loading shift?

Synthetic voltage-control LV network — find the highest-voltage bus at the current operating point and add inductive shunt absorption there. Then power flow noting peak line loading, then a 3-phase short circuit. What's the max ikss?

Baran-Wu 33-bus — identify the most heavily loaded line at the current operating point and reinforce it by paralleling one extra circuit, then drop line 1 out of service. N-1 sweep for all lines; find the contingency causing the worst loading. Mitigate by adding a 22 MW gen at bus 1, then re-run with that worst line out. What's the new peak loading?

Take the IEEE 14-bus case. First spot the line that's working hardest at the current operating point and reinforce it by paralleling one extra circuit — run OPF, note total cost. Then ramp load 3 up by 58% over base and re-run OPF. How does the total cost shift?
CIGRE MV benchmark — find the highest-voltage bus and add inductive shunt absorption there. Power flow noting peak line loading, then a 3-phase short circuit. Max ikss?

Simple MV open ring — find the lowest-voltage bus and add capacitive shunt support there. Run a power flow. If anything exceeds 59.7% loading, also dial load 0 down to 0.8 scaling and re-run. Min bus voltage at the end.

GB reduced 29-bus network — find the largest load and curtail it to low demand. Power flow first for the operating point, then 3-phase short circuit with superposition (pre-fault voltage). ikss at bus 15.

IEEE 24-bus RTS — find the biggest load and curtail it to low demand, and take line 4 out of service. N-1 across all lines; find the worst contingency. Mitigate by adding a 30 MW gen at bus 11, then re-run with that worst line out. New peak line loading?

145-bus case — identify the line working hardest at the current operating point and reinforce it by paralleling one extra circuit. Power flow first to set the operating point, then 3-phase short circuit with superposition. ikss at bus 143 please.
9-bus WSCC case — find the most heavily loaded line and parallel one extra circuit. OPF, note total cost. Then scale load 1 by 1.61 and re-run OPF. Cost difference?

IEEE 24-bus RTS — find the most heavily loaded transformer and bump its tap by one step. N-1 across all lines; identify the worst-loading contingency. Mitigate with a 34 MW gen at bus 3, re-run with the worst line out, and report the new peak line loading.

IEEE 39-bus New England — find the line working hardest at the current operating point and parallel one extra circuit. OPF, lock in the total cost. Then scale load 19 by 1.37 and re-run OPF. By how much does the total cost change?

GB 2224-bus network — find the lowest-voltage load bus and curtail its largest load to low demand. Run a power flow. If anything is over 16.6% loading, set gen 61's active to 384.4 MW and re-run. Final min bus voltage.

In the grid I'm studying a couple of lines are taken out of service during the peak hours of the day and switched back in afterwards. If I step through a day like that, with the load climbing into the peak and then easing off again, what's the worst line loading percentage that turns up at any point across the whole run?

I want to see how far the voltage sags along a low-voltage feeder. If I put together a simple LV radial feeder with a handful of loads spread down the line and solve the power flow, what's the lowest per-unit voltage anywhere on it?

I've got a small feeder with a load at the end, an external grid at the head and a distributed generator partway along. I want to drive that generator's reactive power over a series of steps, sweeping it from absorbing to injecting. As the reactive power ramps up, what's the highest per-unit voltage the generator's own bus reaches across the run?

I'm running a time-series simulation on a network fed through a transformer and I want to capture the results across all the steps as the load grows through the day. Once the whole series has run, what's the highest transformer loading percentage recorded over the run?

I'm testing state estimation. I run a normal power flow first and then feed those results back in as the measurements — bus voltages plus line flows — and run the estimator on a small network. What voltage magnitude does the estimator return at the far end of the feeder?

I'm solving an optimal power flow to minimise generation cost, and I need the external grid at the slack bus to stay within its maximum active-power limit. With the slack capped and the other generators carrying a higher cost, what active power does the external grid settle at?

Is there a way to pull the network's bus admittance matrix out of pandapower? After I solve the power flow on a standard test system, give me the magnitude of the first diagonal entry of that Y-bus matrix.

I'm running a time-series power flow on a low-voltage system where each load follows its own profile over several steps. Once the series has finished, what's the lowest bus voltage seen at any bus across all the time steps?

When I hand pandapower a transformer's nameplate data - the short-circuit voltage, the resistive part of it, iron losses and open-circuit current - it has to turn all that into an internal impedance the solver actually uses. For a 25 MVA 110/20 kV transformer with a 12% short-circuit voltage (0.41% resistive), what is the magnitude of that internally derived per-unit branch impedance?

Is there a built-in way to make several generators share the balancing duty in a plain AC power flow, the way primary frequency response would split it? Set up a small system where two machines share the slack according to participation weights, with the load exceeding what they are scheduled for, and tell me the active power the second, non-reference machine ends up delivering.

I've got a small transmission grid where the neighbouring network is represented by an xward. When I run an AC optimal power flow with bus voltage limits enforced, does the xward bus stay inside the band? Give me the lowest bus voltage in per-unit after the OPF.
Can you run an AC optimal power flow on the IEEE 14-bus system with generator and voltage limits active and give me the total generation cost it settles on?
I have a 24-hour load profile and I want to run an optimal power flow for every hour on the 9-bus case, then report the total generation cost summed over the whole day.

I'm driving a time-series study where the loads follow controllers, but instead of a plain power flow I want each step solved as an optimal power flow. On the 9-bus case, what's the highest line loading seen across all the time steps?
After solving the 9-bus case, I'd like to look at the power-flow Jacobian that the Newton-Raphson used. How many rows does that Jacobian matrix have?
During a time-series optimal power flow I want to log the dispatch cost of each individual time step. Using the 9-bus case over a short horizon, give me the mean per-step dispatch cost.

I want to add an extra linear term to a generator's cost function and see how the optimal objective changes. On the 9-bus case, after bumping generator 1's linear cost coefficient, what's the new total cost from the OPF?
Is there a clean way to tell from a script whether an optimal power flow actually converged? Run the OPF on the 9-bus case and just give me back the converged flag.
I need to call the OPF for a sequence of operating points rather than just once. For the 9-bus case swept across a handful of load levels, how many of those points converge to an optimal solution?

I'd like to add a battery to a small grid and let an optimal power flow decide its charge/discharge. After adding a storage unit with power limits and running the OPF, what active power does the storage end up at?
I'm modelling a corridor with a controllable DC line and I want the optimal power flow to set its transfer. After running the OPF, how much active power flows into the DC line from the sending end?

I've got a couple of static generators (sgens) that I want to make dispatchable in an OPF by giving them a cost. After marking them controllable with a linear cost and running the optimal power flow, what total active power do the sgens provide?

In an OPF, does the external grid still hold the voltage set-point I gave it, or is it free to move within its limits? On the 9-bus case, what voltage does the ext_grid bus come out at after the optimal power flow?
How do I attach a polynomial cost to a generator and have the OPF minimise it? For the 9-bus case, once costs are defined, what active power does generator 1 dispatch at the optimum?
When I run an OPF, how are the active-power limits on the external grid respected versus the generators? On the 9-bus case, give me the external grid's active power at the optimum.

I'm working with the built-in 33-bus distribution case (case33bw) and I want to feed it from a 110 kV source through a transformer instead of the slack sitting directly on bus 0. After adding the HV source and a 110/12.66 kV transformer and running power flow, what loading does that transformer come out at?

I want to stitch a transmission-level network and a distribution-level network together into a single pandapower model (a DSO/TSO setup). After merging the two, how many buses does the combined network have?
Is there an easy way to merge several separate pandapower networks into one? I've got three of them and I'd like the total number of lines in the merged network.

I have a simple grid with a single generator and I want to make sure it never dispatches beyond its rated active-power limit. If I cap the generator and let an optimal power flow decide, what active power does it end up producing?

Is it possible to model part of a grid in DC and tie it back to the AC side? I'd like a DC link built from voltage-source converters and a DC line between two AC areas. After the power flow, what's the lowest DC-bus voltage in per-unit?
If I split a network into two islands by opening the tie between them, can I run a DC power flow on each island separately? I want the line loading on the first line of each island added together.

My network has two transformers and I only want the tap changer on one of them to regulate voltage during the power flow, leaving the other fixed. After the controlled run, what tap position does the regulated transformer settle on?

I'd like the transformer tap changer to hold the voltage on a busbar further down the feeder, not right at the transformer. After letting the tap regulate to a 1.0 pu set-point on the transformer's low side, what voltage does the downstream busbar end up at?

I've got voltage-drop problems along a loaded feeder and want to use the transformer's tap changer to bring the voltages back up. After the tap regulates, what's the lowest bus voltage anywhere on the feeder?
How do I hook a generator up to a bus that already exists in my network? After connecting it and running the power flow, what's the voltage at that generator's bus?

I'm modelling the French extra-high-voltage transmission grid and need to trim it down by removing a set of buses. Starting from the 1354-bus PEGASE case, if I drop buses 100 through 109, how many buses are left?

How do I create a transformer from its explicit resistance, reactance and susceptance data rather than a standard type? After building one from parameters and running the power flow, what's its loading?

When I create a transformer I want to account for its ohmic (copper and iron) losses. After building a transformer with those losses set and running the power flow, how much active power does it lose?

I have two busbars joined by a closed bus-bus switch and I'd like the load-flow current through that switch. With a small impedance on the switch so a current is defined, what current does the power flow report through it?

I'm struggling to specify the parameters for a DC line. Once I set it up between two buses with a given loss percentage and fixed loss, and run the power flow, how much active power actually arrives at the receiving end?

I want to set the voltage angle at the external grid slack and have the power flow honour it. If I give the ext_grid a 5-degree angle and solve with voltage angles enabled, what angle does the neighbouring load bus come out at?

I'm modelling a substation with multiple busbars connected by switches and I need those switches to carry a small impedance (z_ohm) rather than being ideal. After the power flow, what's the voltage difference across the impedant coupler switch?
Can I remove buses from an already-built network? Taking the 30-bus case and deleting a leaf bus together with whatever hangs off it, how many lines remain afterwards?

How do I put a phase-shifting transformer into a simple network? I want a transformer with a 30-degree phase shift in a small loop. After the power flow, how much active power flows through the phase shifter on its HV side?
What does the scaling factor on a generator actually do to the power flow? If I create a generator at 10 MW but give it a scaling of 0.5, what active power does it end up injecting?
Instead of an external grid, I want a generator to act as the slack for my network. If I mark a generator as the slack and run the power flow, what active power does it supply?

How does slack_weight distribute the slack among generators? With two generators carrying slack weights of 1 and 2 and a distributed-slack power flow, what active power does the first generator end up supplying?

On the IEEE European low-voltage test feeder I want to tighten the voltage band and then see how low the bus voltages actually get from an unbalanced power flow. What's the minimum per-phase bus voltage?
In a network with a handful of buses, how do I pull the result for just one specific bus after the power flow? Give me the voltage at bus 5 of the 14-bus case.
How do I find the maximum power flowing through any branch in my network? On the 14-bus case after the power flow, what's the largest active power on any line (sending end)?
How can I tell which way the current is flowing on a line after the power flow? For line 0 of the 9-bus case, give me the signed active power at the from-end so I can read off the direction.
Can pandapower handle a network with more than one slack bus? If I put two external grids on separate buses and run the power flow, what active power does the first external grid supply?

I want the slack to be shared across several generators rather than pinned to one bus. With a distributed-slack power flow over three generators, what total active power do the generators supply together?

I'd like to take a medium-voltage benchmark distribution network, bump one of the loads, and re-run the power flow. On the CIGRE MV network after increasing load 0 by 50%, what's the lowest bus voltage?
I just want the results for one particular bus printed out. After the power flow on the 9-bus case, what is the voltage angle at bus 4?
I'm seeing surprisingly high voltages on a lightly loaded cable feeder. On a long, almost unloaded line, what's the highest bus voltage the power flow reports (the Ferranti-type rise)?
Is the built-in 33-bus distribution case actually radial, or does it have loops in it? Tell me how many independent loops the case33bw topology contains.

I'd like a switched shunt (capacitor bank) whose step gets adjusted over a time series depending on the bus voltage. Running a short horizon on a small feeder, what's the highest shunt step that ends up being selected?

I want to drive the scaling of all my loads from an input dataframe and run a time-series power flow. On the 9-bus case with a load-scaling profile, what's the peak line loading seen across the whole series?

I want to handle the results of a time-series run directly in memory instead of writing them to disk. After a short series on the 9-bus case, give me the mean active power at the slack over all steps, read straight from the in-memory output.
For a time-series study I need to set both active and reactive power per bus at each time step from profiles. On a small feeder driven this way, what's the minimum bus voltage over the whole series?
How do I apply a ConstControl to several load buses at once for a time-series run? With three loads following the same profile, what's the peak total load across the series?

When running a time-series load flow, how do I pass power-flow options (like enabling voltage-angle calculation) through to each step? On the 9-bus case run that way, what's the maximum bus voltage angle seen?

How can I create dispatchable loads that an optimal power flow is allowed to shed for cost? After making a load controllable with a reward for served demand and running the OPF, how much of it is served?
How do I read a specific value out of the network result tables after a power flow? On the 14-bus case, give me the reactive power the external grid injects.
I want to run the European low-voltage test feeder with its three-phase asymmetric loads across a few load levels. What's the lowest per-phase voltage anywhere over that sweep?
Is it possible to get the short-circuit current in a branch for a single-line-to-ground fault? On a small feeder, what fault current shows up at the far bus for a 1-phase fault?
I want to model an unbalanced load and run an asymmetric power flow. With different active powers on each phase at a bus, what's the voltage spread (phase A minus phase C) at that bus?

During a single-phase-to-ground fault, what phase-to-ground voltages do the buses see? On a small MV feeder, give me the maximum bus short-circuit current for a 1-phase fault as the severity indicator.

I'd like to do a voltage sensitivity analysis on a distribution network: how much does a bus voltage move per MW of extra load there? On the CIGRE MV network, give me dV/dP at load bus 0 in pu per MW.

How do I get a PTDF-style sensitivity of a line's flow to an injection at a bus? On the 9-bus case, by how much (MW/MW) does the flow on line 0 change when I inject at bus 4, computed on the DC power flow?
How can I get the R/X ratio at a given bus? On a small feeder, compute the short-circuit R/X ratio seen at the far bus.
How sensitive is a bus voltage to the transformer tap position? Nudging the tap by one step, what's the change in the low-side bus voltage per tap step?

Use the standard Baran–Wu 33-bus radial distribution feeder in its base configuration and multiply both active and reactive power of every existing load by 1.10, leaving all other settings unchanged. Run a balanced AC power flow and report the total active-power loss over all in-service lines in kW.

Use the canonical Baran–Wu IEEE 69-bus radial distribution feeder, with bus numbers referring to the published 1–69 labels and with the exact base-case data frozen with the benchmark. Add a 1.2 MW unity-power-factor PV unit at bus 61, keep the original loads unchanged, run a balanced AC power flow, and report the active power imported from the upstream source at bus 1 in MW, with positive meaning power supplied into the feeder.

Use the CIGRE MV benchmark without DER and retain its default radial switch state, with S1, S2, and S3 open. Represent one +2.5% boost position on both source transformers by setting the equivalent source-side voltage magnitude to 1.025 p.u., hold all other controls fixed, run a balanced AC power flow, and report the minimum voltage magnitude among the in-service 20 kV buses.

On the standard Baran–Wu 33-bus feeder, add an inverter at bus label 18 with a fixed active-power injection of 0.400 MW. Sweep its reactive-power setpoint from −2000 to +2000 kvar in 1 kvar increments, run a balanced AC power flow at each setpoint, and select the converged setpoint that minimizes the absolute deviation of the bus-18 voltage from 1.000 p.u.; if tied, choose the smaller numerical setpoint. Report the selected reactive-power setpoint in kvar, with positive denoting injection into the network.

Use the CIGRE LV benchmark and identify residential loads as the existing load elements whose names begin with “Load R.” At each residential load bus, add a unity-power-factor PV unit whose rated active power equals that load’s original active power, then independently solve two balanced AC power-flow scenarios in which every original load and every added PV are scaled by (0.45, 0.90) and (0.80, 0.20), respectively. Report the highest voltage magnitude over all in-service 0.4 kV buses and both scenarios.

Use the CIGRE MV benchmark without DER and close the three normally open line switches S1, S2, and S3, leaving all other statuses unchanged. Run a balanced AC power flow, select the in-service line with the highest loading percentage, breaking an exact tie by the smallest line-record index, take that line out of service, and rerun the power flow. Define total active-power loss as the sum over all in-service lines and transformers, and report 100 × (post-outage loss − pre-outage loss) / pre-outage loss.

Use the standard Baran–Wu 33-bus radial feeder with its original loads and branch statuses. At bus label 30, connect a fixed-admittance shunt capacitor rated to supply 600 kvar at 1.0 p.u., run a balanced AC power flow, and report the voltage magnitude at bus 30.

Use the built-in IEEE 14-bus case and take the sole generator at bus 2 out of service while leaving that bus and its load in service. Keep every other generator at its original active-power and voltage setpoints, let the external grid at bus 1 balance the system, run an AC power flow without enforcing generator reactive-power limits, and report the voltage magnitude at bus 14.

Use the built-in IEEE 30-bus case and increase both active and reactive demand of every load at bus 7 by 25%, leaving all other data unchanged. Solve an AC optimal power flow with the case’s original generation costs, generator P/Q limits, bus-voltage limits, and branch limits, then report the optimized total generation cost in the case’s native cost units per hour.

Use the built-in IEEE 39-bus case and run the base AC power flow with the original generator active-power and voltage setpoints, without enforcing reactive-power limits. Among in-service line elements whose individual removal leaves all in-service buses connected, select the line with the largest loading, defined as the larger terminal-current magnitude divided by rated current, breaking a tie by the smallest line-record index. Open that line, rerun the AC power flow, and report the highest loading of the remaining line elements under the same definition, excluding transformers.

Use the built-in IEEE RTS-79 24-bus case and examine exactly 38 single-branch outages: each of its 33 lines and 5 two-winding transformers once. For each outage, require the remaining network to be connected and solve an AC optimal power flow with all original generation costs and P/Q, voltage, and branch constraints and no load shedding; count an outage as feasible only when the optimization terminates successfully and satisfies those constraints. After all outages have been examined, report the largest optimized total generation cost among the feasible outages in native cost units per hour, or −1.0 if none is feasible.

Use the built-in IEEE 57-bus case and test λ = 1.00, 1.01, …, 2.00 in ascending order; at each value multiply every load’s active and reactive demand by λ, retain the base active-power and voltage setpoints of all non-slack generators, enforce their original reactive-power limits, and let the external grid balance the system. For each λ, test the 62 single-line outages whose individual removal leaves the original network connected, keeping all transformers in service; a value fails if any contingency power flow does not converge, any in-service bus voltage lies outside 0.95–1.05 p.u., or any remaining line’s larger terminal-current-to-rated-current ratio exceeds 100%. Return the largest passing λ, return 0.00 if λ = 1.00 fails, and return 2.00 if every tested value passes.

Use the built-in IEEE 9-bus case and increase only the linear coefficient of the active-power polynomial cost of the sole generator at bus 2 by 30%, leaving its constant and quadratic coefficients and every other input unchanged. Solve a DC optimal power flow with the original generator and branch active-power limits, then report that generator’s optimized active-power output.

Use the built-in IEEE 118-bus case and run a base AC power flow, then select the online non-slack generator with the largest active-power output, breaking a tie by the smallest bus label and then the smallest generator-record index. Take that generator out of service and redistribute its pre-contingency MW once among the remaining online non-slack generators in proportion to each unit’s upward reserve, defined as original maximum active power minus base active-power output; exclude the external grid at bus 69 from this allocation and let it supply only losses and numerical allocation residual. Keep the remaining generators’ original voltage setpoints, enforce their original reactive-power limits, rerun the AC power flow, and report the greatest loading among line elements only, defined as the larger terminal-current magnitude divided by rated current.

Use the CIGRE MV benchmark without DER and retain its default switch states. Set the external grid’s maximum short-circuit power to 500 MVA and maximum-case R/X ratio to 0.1, apply a zero-impedance three-phase fault at the 20 kV Bus 11, and under the IEC 60909 maximum short-circuit case report the initial symmetrical short-circuit current at Bus 11.

Use the built-in IEEE 14-bus network and treat only the external grid at Bus 1 as a short-circuit source, with maximum short-circuit power 5000 MVA and maximum-case R/X ratio 0.1; exclude all other generators from short-circuit infeed. For a zero-impedance three-phase fault at Bus 9, calculate the IEC 60909 maximum initial symmetrical current I through the 4–9 transformer on its Bus 4 high-voltage side. Assuming I > Ip, with Ip = 0.05 kA and a time multiplier of 0.15, report t = 0.14 × 0.15 / ((I/Ip)^0.02 − 1).

Run a base-case AC power flow on the built-in IEEE 14-bus network and create synthetic measurements consisting of voltage magnitude and active and reactive bus injection at every bus, line from-end active and reactive flow for every line, and high-voltage-end active and reactive flow for every transformer. Use the load-reference sign convention for bus injections and exclude fixed-shunt consumption from those measurements because the shunt remains represented in the network admittance; use the power-flow values without noise except for adding 0.03 p.u. to the Bus 14 voltage measurement, with standard deviations of 0.005 p.u., 1 MW, and 1 Mvar for voltage, active power, and reactive power, respectively. Run flat-start weighted least-squares state estimation and report the estimated Bus 14 voltage magnitude.

Run a base-case AC power flow on the built-in IEEE 14-bus network and create noiseless synthetic measurements consisting of voltage magnitude and active and reactive bus injection at every bus, line from-end active and reactive flow for every line, and high-voltage-end active and reactive flow for every transformer. Use the load-reference sign convention for bus injections, exclude fixed-shunt consumption from those measurements because the shunt remains represented in the network admittance, and add a +20 MW error only to the Bus 4 high-voltage-side active-power-flow measurement of the 4–9 transformer; use standard deviations of 0.005 p.u., 1 MW, and 1 Mvar. Run a flat-start weighted least-squares estimate, score each measurement by its absolute post-estimation residual divided by its stated standard deviation, remove the measurement with the largest score while breaking a tie by the smallest measurement-table index, rerun from a flat start, and report the Bus 14 voltage angle relative to Bus 1.

Use the built-in Baran–Wu 33-bus radial distribution network in its default topology. For each integer hour h = 0, …, 23, independently scale both active and reactive power of every load by 0.75 + 0.35 sin²(π(h − 6)/24) and run a balanced AC power flow. Report the lowest voltage magnitude observed over all 24 hours and all buses except the external-grid bus.

Use the built-in IEEE 14-bus network and test load multipliers from 1.00 through 5.00 in increments of 0.01, scaling every load’s active and reactive power by the same multiplier. At each step, run a Newton–Raphson AC power flow from a flat start with a 50-iteration limit, enforce the original reactive-power limits of all non-slack generators, and leave the external-grid reactive output unconstrained. Stop at the first step that does not converge or has any bus voltage below 0.70 p.u. and report the preceding multiplier; if no step fails through 5.00, report 5.00.
